subject: Post-call: SDK enablement lab & local smoke validation for BrightPath

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-call: SDK enablement lab & local smoke validation for BrightPath

Evan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so the team has a single place to follow up.

Recap (what we heard)
- BrightPath wants a lightweight SDK quickstart (Python + TS) developers can run locally behind your C.I. or inside your VPC dev subnet.
- Auth preference: short-term: API key for PoC, long-term: OIDC + KMS integration.
- Required features: structured output (JSON schema enforcement / tool-calling), embeddings for search indexing, and a lightweight reranker for top-k results.
- Non-functional: expected steady-state throughput ~50 req/s, short-tail latency target < 300ms for user-facing chat.

Immediate ask / mutual action plan
1) We will send a starter sample repo (Python + TS) with an auth switch (API key vs OIDC stub) and routing examples for model variants. (Grace) — target delivery: Wed 14 Apr.
2) BrightPath to confirm whether the PoC will run in a public dev subnet or strictly VPC-only (Evan).
3) Karthik to produce a short runbook for local testing: env vars, token routing, and how to flip on embeddings + reranker locally. (Karthik) — target: Thu 15 Apr.
4) Security questionnaire: Evan will share a minimal SOC/KMS requirement doc; we will answer and attach sample infra diagrams. (Evan + Redwood)

Attachments we will provide: sdks-sampleapp.zip (starter apps), redwood-routing-arch.png (suggested network + routing), security-questions.xlsx (security checklist).

Proposed follow-up: Technical deep-dive Friday 16 Apr, 9:00–10:00am PT — we'll demo the local quickstart and walk through OIDC vs API key flows. If that doesn't work, please propose two alternate times.

Notes for engineering: sample repo will include two quick tests — a local smoke that posts a prompt and asserts a JSON schema response, and an embeddings index + rerank smoke that runs with small in-memory docs.

Thanks,
Grace

Thanks Grace — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- PoC environment: must be VPC-only (we cannot hit external public endpoints from dev network during the PoC). We can run the quickstart inside an isolated dev subnet that has egress through our NAT / proxy.
- Auth: API key for quick validation is fine, but we need the OIDC roadmap documented. Can you include a short example of OIDC token exchange and how Redwood suggests integrating with our gateway?
- Data residency: all logs must be configurable to avoid persisting raw user messages to external logs during PoC.
- Throughput: 50 req/s steady; we may see spikes to 120 req/s during batch reindexing. If you have suggested batching/queueing config, include that.

I'll attach the minimal security checklist (separate email). Please send the starter repo and we will run the local smoke in our dev subnet and report back results.

—Evan
Evan Liu
Platform Engineering, BrightPath

Thanks — wrote up the short dev checklist and a first-pass runbook below. I'll attach the sample artifacts and a tiny local test harness.

Quick dev runbook (local smoke)
- Prereqs: python3.10, node16, virtualenv, yarn, git
- Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples.git && cd samples/brightpath-starter
- Env: copy .env.example -> .env (set REDWOOD_API_KEY or set OIDC_STUB=true + OIDC_CLIENT_ID).
- Start (Python): cd python && pip install -r requirements.txt && python smoke_test.py --prompt "Find policy references"
- Start (TS): cd ts && yarn && yarn start:smoke (runs a Node script that uses the TS SDK and asserts schema)
- Embeddings/reranker locally: run index_local.py to build an in-memory FAISS index (small), then reranker_test.py posts top-10 and asserts rerank improves relevance by simple heuristic.
- Routing example: we include a routing.json showing how to route to a retriever-optimized variant for long contexts and a low-latency small model for chat.

Security/dev notes
- For VPC-only PoC: the sample includes a proxy config file to route traffic through your NAT; the SDK accepts an HTTP_PROXY env var.
- Logs: sample uses REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL and REDWOOD_PII_STRIP=true to avoid persisting full user text by default.

Attachments (stubs): sdks-sampleapp.zip (contains samples + smoke_test harness), security-questions.xlsx (filled where we can), redwood-routing-arch.png (network diagram).

I'll push the starter branch by EOD and drop a link here.

- Karthik
